entry.title: feat(progress): add streaks, level estimation, and a placement quiz
entry.content:
feat(progress): add streaks, level estimation, and a placement quiz

Implements M3 (Progress, Streaks & Levels):

- Schema: User.timezone, Streak.lastActiveDate as a plain date string
  (not DateTime, to sidestep timezone-conversion bugs), and
  LessonCompletion.durationSeconds
- src/server/streak.ts: pure date-math streak-transition logic
  (consecutive-day increment, one freeze earned per 7 active days,
  one freeze covers exactly one missed day, larger gaps break the
  streak even with freezes banked) — kept separate from the database
  specifically so it could be unit-tested directly before ever
  touching a router
- src/server/level-estimate.ts: a first-pass, explicitly-directional
  level heuristic (known-word count + "completed >=2 lessons at a
  level comfortably")
- Wired both into progress.completeLesson, which now also updates a
  real streak and level estimate on every lesson completion; added
  progress.getDashboard and a /dashboard page
- Added /placement, a short quiz feeding placement.submit —
  deliberately scoped to only distinguish A1 from A2, since the
  library only has A1 content seeded so far
- Fixed a real bug caught live in the browser: an ordinary lesson
  completion was silently overwriting a placement-quiz result
  downward. completeLesson now takes the higher of the fresh
  heuristic result and the existing estimate (maxLevel()), so only a
  fresh placement attempt can lower it, not routine word-count noise
- Documented the local dev database's recurring flakiness more
  precisely in CLAUDE.md: `prisma dev ls` reporting "running" doesn't
  mean the connection is healthy, and `prisma dev start` doesn't
  reliably revive a broken instance — remove and recreate it instead

entry.title: feat(reader): add synced reader, tap-to-translate, and offline queue
entry.content:
feat(reader): add synced reader, tap-to-translate, and offline queue

Implements M2 (Reader/Player Core) at /learn/[id]:

- Synced text+audio reader (Reader.tsx): segment highlighting keyed to
  audio.currentTime against each segment's startMs/endMs, native
  playback controls plus a speed selector, A-/A+ text size, and a
  translation toggle for A1 bilingual scaffolding
- Tap-to-translate (WordSpan.tsx): a popover that looks up and saves
  the word in one action, never navigating away from the lesson
- Comprehension check (ComprehensionQuiz.tsx) that scores answers and
  records a LessonCompletion via a new progress router
- Offline-tolerant queueing (offlineQueue.ts, localStorage-backed) for
  word-saves and lesson completions per PRD §11 — verified by patching
  window.fetch to fail tRPC calls in the live browser, confirming the
  queue, then confirming it flushes and persists on reconnect

Two architecture fixes made along the way:

- Statically importing @/auth (next-auth) anywhere a router file
  touches broke every test under Vitest, since next-auth requires the
  real Next.js runtime. Fixed by resolving userId once in
  createTRPCContext() and lazily `await import()`-ing @/auth inside
  current-user.ts, so router files and tests never load it. Existing
  tests updated to pass `{ db, userId }` context directly.
- Vitest's parallel test-file workers were corrupting Postgres's
  prepared-statement protocol across files sharing one local
  connection pool. Fixed with fileParallelism: false.

Also fixes a UX bug caught during offline testing: the tap-to-translate
popover showed the same "No definition yet" message for a genuinely
missing word and a failed lookup request. Now distinguishes them.

src/server/current-user.ts falls back to a seeded local-dev user when
no session exists (hard-disabled in production) so known-word/lesson-
completion persistence could be built and tested now rather than
stubbed until M4 ships real sign-in — logged as a follow-up to replace.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: fix(ci): generate Prisma client before typecheck, not after
entry.content:
fix(ci): generate Prisma client before typecheck, not after

Both npm run verify and the CI workflow ran typecheck before
db:generate. This only worked locally because a Prisma client from
earlier manual testing was still sitting in the gitignored
src/generated/prisma — a genuinely fresh checkout (i.e. real CI) has
no client on disk until it's generated, so the first push of M1's
work failed CI immediately on a missing-module error.

Confirmed fixed by deleting src/generated locally and re-running
verify clean.

entry.title: feat(content): add lesson data model, admin panel, and starter content
entry.content:
feat(content): add lesson data model, admin panel, and starter content

Implements M1 (Content Model & Admin Panel):

- Prisma schema covering the full domain model: User, Lesson,
  TranscriptSegment, ComprehensionQuestion, LessonCompletion,
  KnownWord, Streak, LevelEstimate, and LexiconEntry
- Prisma 7 requires an explicit driver adapter now rather than reading
  DATABASE_URL implicitly — wired @prisma/adapter-pg into src/server/db.ts
- src/server/storage.ts: local-disk file storage for lesson audio/cover
  art, standing in for Cloudflare R2 until that account exists; callers
  only ever see saveUpload() and an /api/media/... URL, never a path,
  so swapping backends later won't touch call sites
- tRPC lesson router (create/update/delete/list/getById) and an admin
  panel (/admin/lessons) to author lessons end-to-end, tested working
  in-browser against the real local database. No auth in front of it
  yet — follow-up logged in docs/TASKS.md
- tRPC lexicon router backing tap-to-translate, seeded with 72
  hand-curated French-English entries; bulk-importing a full open
  dataset (FreeDict/Wiktionary) is a follow-up rather than rushed —
  FreeDict's own distributions are TEI XML/StarDict binary, not a
  quick fetch
- 4 real A1 mini-stories written and seeded (prisma/seed.ts), built
  from a shared ~70-word vocabulary with comprehension questions.
  Audio stays null — recording narration needs an actual human voice

Also: the lesson/lexicon router tests are integration tests against
the real local database rather than mocked, so npm run verify and CI
now push the schema and seed data before running tests, and CI gained
a real Postgres service container.

entry.title: build(ci): add pre-commit quality gate and Conventional Commits
entry.content:
build(ci): add pre-commit quality gate and Conventional Commits

Every commit now runs `npm run verify` via Husky before it's allowed:
format check, lint, dependency-tree check, a security-audit check,
typecheck, unit tests, and a full production build. Any failure
blocks the commit.

`npm audit` is gated through scripts/check-audit.mjs rather than
called directly, because npm's --omit=dev does not actually exclude
devDependencies from the audit graph (a known npm limitation) — used
plain, this would permanently fail every commit on 4 high-severity
advisories that live entirely inside Prisma CLI's own bundled MySQL
introspection tooling (dev-only, unreachable in this Postgres-only
project, no fix available short of downgrading Prisma two majors).
The script fails on anything high/critical that isn't on its
reviewed, dated allowlist, so a genuinely new vulnerability still
blocks a commit.

Also adds commitlint + a commit-msg hook enforcing Conventional
Commits, and .gitattributes forcing LF on .husky/* and *.sh so a
Windows checkout doesn't corrupt the hook scripts with CRLF.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Complete M0 code-side setup: tRPC, Prisma, Auth.js, CI, tests
entry.content:
Complete M0 code-side setup: tRPC, Prisma, Auth.js, CI, tests

Finishes the parts of M0 (Project Foundations) that don't require
creating an external account:

- ESLint + Prettier + strict TypeScript, wired together
- tRPC end to end (Next.js route handler, React Query client provider,
  a health.ping procedure proving the wiring works)
- Prisma installed and verified against a local database via
  `prisma dev` (no Docker or account needed for local work); pinned
  to the stable 7.10.0 release after `npm install` initially resolved
  a v8 release-candidate tagged "latest" on npm
- Auth.js v5 scaffolded with Google + Resend magic-link providers,
  inactive until real credentials are supplied
- GitHub Actions CI: lint, format check, typecheck, unit tests, build
  on every push/PR
- Vitest and Playwright configured with passing smoke tests
- Fixed a typecheck gotcha: Next.js 16's generated route types
  (LayoutProps etc.) don't exist until `next typegen` runs, so
  `npm run typecheck` now runs it first — otherwise a clean checkout
  or CI run fails typecheck before ever building

Still blocked on Aira creating accounts: hosted Postgres
(Neon/Supabase), Cloudflare R2, Vercel, Sentry, PostHog — all noted
in docs/TASKS.md.
